newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore court finds politician guilty of libel.
newsitem.headline: Singapore court finds politician guilty of libel.

text.p: Singapore's High Court on Monday found an opposition politician guilty of libeling Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and other ruling party members during an election campaign in December.
Justice Goh Joon Seng said Tang Liang Hong, who fled abroad shortly after the polls, had presented no defence and therefore found in favour of the ruling People's Action Party (PAP) litigants.
Justice Goh, who is not related to the prime minister, said he would set a date later for a hearing to determine the damages and costs Tang would have to pay.
Tang unsuccessfully stood for the Worker's Party in January 2 general elections in which the PAP won 81 of parliament's 83 seats.

The PAP, led by the prime minister, accused Tang of being a "Chinese chauvinist" who threatened racial harmony in Singapore. Tang called them liars and was hit by a deluge of 12 libel suits from PAP leaders who said they had to defend their integrity.
